questions.answer: Waterfall, incremental development, spiral, reuse-oriented and prototype models

questions.question: What is the aim of the Layered Architecture experiment?
questions.answer: To implement a Student Management System using the layered (N-tier) architecture, separating the presentation, business logic and data access layers

questions.question: What does LRU stand for and which entry does it evict?
questions.answer: Least Recently Used; it removes the entry that has not been used for the longest time

questions.question: What is the aim of experiment 15?
questions.answer: To compare the response time of an application with and without caching and measure the improvement

questions.question: How is demand defined in the notes?
questions.answer: The quantity of a commodity consumers are willing to buy at a given price

questions.question: What is inventory?
questions.answer: Stock of materials kept for future use

questions.question: Why doesn't a change in one layer affect the whole layered system?
questions.answer: Because every layer has one responsibility and only talks to the layer directly below it, so changes don't ripple through the system

questions.question: What does the Controller do in the MVC architecture?
questions.answer: It receives the user's action, asks the model to update, and selects what the view must show

questions.question: Why does the LRU cache use dummy head and tail nodes?
questions.answer: They are sentinels at both ends of the doubly linked list

questions.question: What happens when a producer tries to put a message in a full bounded queue?
questions.answer: put() waits until there is room

questions.question: What happens in the HALF-OPEN state?
questions.answer: One trial call is allowed; if it succeeds the circuit closes, otherwise it opens again

questions.question: What is the difference between technical and economic efficiency?
questions.answer: Technical efficiency is producing maximum output from given resources; economic efficiency is producing the desired output at minimum possible cost

questions.question: When should a project be accepted under the rate of return method?
questions.answer: When IRR > MARR; reject when IRR < MARR

questions.question: Why are traditional cybersecurity tools hard for ordinary users, according to the FraudAlert introduction?
questions.answer: They are designed for technically proficient users and demand an advanced understanding of security concepts

questions.question: How is FraudAlert different from existing tools?
questions.answer: It combines message analysis, URL verification, fraud scoring, JWT accounts, community reporting and scam analytics in one platform, instead of addressing one dimension

questions.question: Where does the FraudAlert client put the JWT on later requests?
questions.answer: In the Authorization header

questions.question: What did the FraudAlert reporting system achieve in testing?
questions.answer: Users could submit scam reports and all reports were persisted to MongoDB Atlas
